script.base: Market says KC leads (implied 26.2-20.2). Walker is the script: 23 carries for 173 in week 1 into an IND run defense that allowed 6.03 YPC and 6 runs of 10+, so KC should lean run, lead by the second half, and hand Walker the late carries. IND (Daniel Jones 1 rush/4 yards) trails and throws more; Taylor's 19-carry week-1 role is the volume at risk. Total 46.5 is moderate, not a shootout and not a 6-point blowout flag, so starters should finish.
script.flip1: Game stays inside one score. Taylor keeps a full carry share (he already had 19), KC cannot just clock-kill, and Mahomes has to throw, which lifts Worthy/Kelce/Rice and caps Walker's carry pile-up.
script.flip2: KC scores early and the game gets to two scores. IND abandons the run entirely (Taylor rush dies), Jones is forced into KC's 30% blitz (IND EPA/db vs blitz -0.95), and Walker/Johnson own the second half on the ground while IND pass-catchers only get garbage volume.

pre_mortem: Monday the Taylor under lost because the game stayed within a score, Giddens was inactive, Jones sat with the calf, and Taylor got 20-plus carries plus one 15-yard run against a front that was not the week-1 unit — a 6-point spread is not a blowout and 98.5 is only a half-yard above last week. The Worthy over lost because KC did hand Walker the game, Worthy saw 3 targets and another miss on his air yards, and IND's 17 YPA left was one bad opponent rather than a scheme hole we never charted. Weather was never saved; wind at Arrowhead would have been another way the deep shot died. If those counters are how you see it, both leans should be passed, not upgraded.
slip_story: One story: KC leads but does not bury them. Taylor under belongs to the dog-throws / sturdy-KC-front stack. Worthy over belongs to the same script only if Mahomes still takes the 5-6 shots he took in Walker's 173-yard week-1 game against a secondary that just bled explosives. Do not add Walker over 173.5, Pierce over 61.5, Kelce over 71.5, or a total over — those need either an outlier repeat or the opposite efficiency environment. No TD legs. One market per player.
